verdict.rationale: Context.dev has its own crawl capability. The synchronous crawl returns page Markdown in one response but is capped at 500 pages and framed as a 'small website section'. Larger crawls of up to 25,000 pages run as an async background batch that needs progress tracking and a separate retrieval step, so 'entire website in one request' holds only within that cap or across multiple calls. missing for 10: single-request coverage of whole sites beyond 500 pages, independent or hands-on corroboration of full-site crawl completeness (the SiteGPT migration is a vendor-published claim).

support.subject: As a developer, I can crawl an entire website and get content from all its pages with one request

citations.quote: Crawl a small website section and return page Markdown in one response, with a maximum of 500 pages.
Crawl up to 25,000 pages in a background batch, track progress, and retrieve Markdown or HTML when the job finishes.
Scrape 25K URLs or crawl large websites asynchronously.
switched from Firecrawl to Context.dev to scrape entire websites and turn them into the knowledge base behind its customers' bots
